title: QFBench 2.0 Track-4 tabular-prediction output (answer.json)
description: Reasoning-augmented tabular prediction over entity rows. A unit may be classification (predict a label per entity), regression (predict a numeric value per entity), or ranking (order entities by a predicted score). One prediction per entity row lives in entity_predictions[]. Every prediction must carry >=1 evidence-grounded claim, and every claim cites a span in the frozen corpus; gate g3 runs the ensemble-NLI faithfulness judge and resolves each cited doc's date from the corpus for the embargo check. The card's target_type declares which task applies for this unit.

target_type.description: Declares the prediction task; must match the card's target_type.

entity_predictions.description: One prediction per entity row in q.json.

label.description: Predicted class for classification tasks (e.g. 'beat'/'miss'/'inline', 'credit_event'/'no_event'). Optional for regression/ranking.

point_forecast.description: Predicted value for regression, or the rank score for ranking. Optional confidence for classification.

rank.description: 1-based predicted rank for ranking tasks (1 = highest).

interval.description: 90% prediction interval. Required for every entity and all target_type values.

claims.description: Evidence-grounded claims supporting this entity's prediction. Each claim bundles its text and one corpus citation.

doc_id.description: ID of a document in the frozen corpus, or "task" for the unit's task table (Track 4 scorer 5.2.0: a span inside the citing entity's own row of the task table). A corpus document's doc_date is resolved from the corpus for the embargo gate (must be <= question cutoff).

allOf.description: ranking entities carry a point_forecast (the rank score).

evidence_trace.description: Free-text reasoning trace, or ordered doc_ids the agent retrieved/used.

notes.description: Optional free-form author notes (ignored by the scorer).

submitted_reasons.description: Optional. Up to three reasons for the answer, read by the reasoning grader (an LLM judge panel, separate from the analysis score and the faithfulness gate). Omit the field to submit no reasons; a missing reason scores 0 against every target reason. The judge sees each reason's premise, mechanism and answer_implication and the corpus text its citations resolve to, never scope or the raw citations. Published caps, per unit, over which the unit's reasoning is not judged and scores 0 (never clipped): each citation span_end - span_start <= 8000 characters; and three caps in UTF-8 bytes of the compact JSON the judge reads: your per-entity answer (entity_id and the declared answer fields) <= 3000 bytes, your reasons (reason_id, premise, mechanism, answer_implication) <= 6500 bytes, the cited passages (each passage's text with its doc_id, span_start, span_end and the reason_id citing it) <= 46500 bytes (together 56000 bytes). A reason with the same premise, mechanism and answer_implication as an earlier one is not judged. Citations resolve against the corpus only (doc_id "task" is for claims). Participant-written text must not contain the published deny-list phrases (URLs, file paths, identity or other-submission references); a premise that is wholly a verbatim quote of a corpus document is exempt.

mechanism.description: Why that fact moves the answer.

answer_implication.description: What the fact implies for the submitted answer, naming the entities.

scope.description: Optional. The entities this reason is about. Not shown to the judge.

entities.description: entity_id values from the task's roster.

citations.description: Optional. Corpus passages behind this reason, in the same character-offset convention as claims. A citation that does not resolve in the frozen corpus, or whose document is dated after the cutoff, is never shown to the judge.
